text:
Market context
Adoption has grown for three years but the gap to peers is widening












Index, 2021 = 12


Key drivers

Tooling became cheap enough to trial without a business case
Procurement cycles shortened from nine months to about six weeks
Internal champions replaced central mandates


The gap is a distribution problem, not a capability one.



Note: Index rebased to 2021.   Source: Internal benchmark; sector survey 2025


This is the standard workhorse slide: chart left at 55%, narrative right at 45%, each column with its own noun-phrase header. Read the action title aloud and the chart should be the proof of exactly that sentence — nothing more.

By the numbers
Four figures set the scale of the opportunity


82 M€ Cost saved


16 Countries


2 450 Employees


~6 wks Time to value



Every figure on this slide is sourced below. A number without a base is decoration.


Source: Nexer Group annual report 2025; PostNord engagement summary


The big-number row is lifted from the Nexer corporate deck. Keep it to four at most — a fifth turns it into a table and the eye stops ranking them.

Options
Three routes are open, and they differ mainly in who carries the risk









Route
What it involves
Risk sits with
Time to value




Pilot first
One team, one workflow, fixed scope
Nexer
~6 weeks


Platform first
Build shared tooling, then onboard teams
Shared
~6 months


Buy and adapt
Licence a vendor product, configure it
Client
~3 months




Note: Time to value measured from contract signature to first production use.


Options tables are for decisions, not inventories. Three rows, one differentiating column — here it is who carries the risk. If every column differs, you have not found the real trade-off yet.

text:
Bridge
Two thirds of the saving comes from a single lever


€ millions, annualised


Note: Figures rounded to the nearest million; totals may not sum.   Source: Engagement model v4


A bridge answers “where does the number come from”. Label the start bar, the end bar, and every step between — an unlabelled segment is an invitation to be asked about it.

title: Deck title goes here
text:
Recommendation
Start with one workflow, prove it in six weeks, then decide on the platform

Weeks 1–2 — pick the workflow with the clearest baseline and the least integration
Weeks 3–5 — build in the open, with the receiving team in the room
Week 6 — measure against the baseline; publish the result either way


The decision this deck asks for is the six-week pilot, not the platform.

Detail on the pilot

Close on the ask, stated as one sentence, with the timeline that makes it credible. Everything else belongs in the appendix.
